Michigan is not one of the three states (Connecticut, New Jersey, New York) the document's own footnote and symbol legend name as having a Prior-Authorization fallback for bare 'E' items -- so in Michigan an 'E'-only listing means excluded from coverage outright, not PA-eligible. records.verificationNote: Fetched https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/resources/pharmacy/commercial-pdl-jan-2026.pdf directly (WebFetch's own summarizer returned only a 'corrupted/encoded' message per this repo's known uhcprovider.com quirk, but the tool result named the local path where it had already saved the raw PDF bytes; opening that path with PyMuPDF/fitz yielded full readable text across all 80 pages). Page 1 (0-indexed) confirms the document is UnitedHealthcare's '2026 Prescription Drug List,' Effective January 1, 2026, publisher 'UnitedHealthcare & affiliated companies.' The document names no state carve-out other than CT, NJ and NY. The 'Metabolic Bone Disease Agents - Drugs for Osteoporosis' section (page footer '44', 0-indexed page 43) lists verbatim: alendronate sodium oral tablet (Tier 1, no flags), FOSAMAX (Tier 4), ibandronate sodium oral (Tier 2), risedronate sodium oral tablet 150mg/35mg (Tier 3, QL) and 30mg/5mg (Tier 3, no flag), and ACTONEL (E, QL). Page 4 (0-indexed) supplies the symbol legend: 'E: May be excluded from coverage or subject to Prior Authorization in Connecticut, New Jersey and New York' -- since Michigan is not named in that carve-out, a bare 'E' flag (no separate PA flag) means straightforward exclusion from coverage in Michigan. Alendronate tablet is the only oral bisphosphonate at Tier 1 with zero flags, so it was selected as the class-level preferred agent -- the PDL itself does not use an explicit 'preferred agent' label, so this single-agent selection is a judgment call from the tier/flag pattern, though the underlying tier/flag data for every named agent is verbatim-verified. The representative 70mg once-weekly strength and directions are standard FDA-label prescribing convention, not stated in the PDL (which lists drug names/tiers/flags only, no dosing guidance). [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]

records.preferredRestriction: Not listed anywhere on the outpatient pharmacy PDL -- this agent is an in-office/infusion-center administered drug, and the PDL explicitly states its scope 'does not include ... medications obtained or administered in a physician's office.' Zoledronic acid for osteoporosis is billed under UHC's medical benefit (HCPCS J3489), not the OptumRx pharmacy benefit, so no PDL tier or pharmacy PA-notification document applies to it the way one does for self-administered/specialty-pharmacy drugs in this class list.
records.verificationNote: The cited 2026 Prescription Drug List (effective 2026-01-01, publisher UnitedHealthcare & affiliated companies) is the correct, current pharmacy formulary for this payer/state -- a full-document keyword search across all 80 pages for 'zoledronic', 'reclast', and the HCPCS code 'J3489' returned zero hits, confirming zoledronic acid/Reclast is genuinely absent from the pharmacy PDL rather than missed, consistent with the PDL's own stated scope exclusion for physician-office-administered drugs (page 3, 0-indexed). The document names no state carve-out other than CT, NJ and NY. A follow-up WebSearch located UnitedHealthcare's 'Maximum Dosage and Frequency - Commercial Medical Benefit Drug Policy' (effective 2026-01-01), which lists Reclast's maximum dose (5 mg per administration, HCPCS J3489) but is a dosage-ceiling policy, not a dedicated prior-authorization policy for the drug -- it does not state whether PA is required. No dedicated UHC commercial medical-benefit PA policy specifically for zoledronic acid/Reclast (mirroring the ones confirmed for Denosumab and Evenity in the sibling rankl-inhibitor and anabolic classes) could be located via WebSearch. General industry practice and UHC's own parallel osteoporosis medical-benefit policies (Denosumab, Evenity) both require prior authorization for infused/injected antiresorptive and anabolic bone agents, making PA a reasonable inference for zoledronic acid as well, but this specific requirement is NOT confirmed against a UHC-commercial-specific document and is marked accordingly. The representative dosing (5mg/100mL, annual/biennial IV infusion) is standard FDA-label information, not sourced from a UHC document. [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]

records.preferredRestriction: Prior authorization is required for every denosumab product, including the preferred Prolia and Stoboclo, per UHC's Commercial Medical Benefit Drug Policy for Denosumab (Policy 2026D0068T, effective 7/1/2026 -- this is a national commercial policy with no state-specific carve-out). Initial authorization is limited to 12 months at a time and requires: diagnosis of osteoporosis (or glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis), patient at high risk of fracture (history of osteoporotic fracture, multiple risk factors, or failure/intolerance of other available therapy), and FDA-labeled dosing. Reauthorization requires documented positive clinical response, also capped at 12 months per approval.
records.boglNote: Prolia (denosumab) and its FDA-approved biosimilar Stoboclo (denosumab-bmwo) are both named as the co-preferred denosumab products in this policy -- this is not a brand-over-generic scenario since the branded originator (Prolia) is itself one of the two preferred options, on equal footing with its biosimilar.

Page 1 confirms verbatim: 'UnitedHealthcare Commercial Medical Benefit Drug Policy, Denosumab, Policy Number: 2026D0068T, Effective Date: July 1, 2026.' records.preferredRestriction: Prior authorization plus specialty pharmacy dispensing required even for TYMLOS, despite its Tier 3 placement on the PDL (flags 'PA, SP'). Per UHC's dedicated Tymlos Prior Authorization/Notification program (2025 P 1222-11, effective 12/1/2025 -- a national commercial pharmacy program with no state-specific carve-out), approval requires a diagnosis of postmenopausal (or male) osteoporosis AND either high fracture risk (recent fracture, multiple risk factors, very low T-score, high fall risk, or high FRAX score) OR documented failure/intolerance/contraindication to another osteoporosis therapy. Cumulative lifetime use is capped at 2 years (24 months) across ALL parathyroid hormone analogs combined (abaloparatide + teriparatide), per UHC policy and AACE/ACE and Endocrine Society guidance cited in the same document.

alternatives.note: Tier 3, PA, SP -- same restriction tier as Tymlos; approved under UHC's parallel teriparatide PA program (2025 P 1033-17, eff 11/1/2025); shares the same 24-month lifetime cap across all parathyroid hormone analogs

paRequired.reason: Marked 'E, PA, SP' on the PDL -- the explicit PA flag applies nationally (it is not part of the CT/NJ/NY-only carve-out that governs bare 'E' listings), so Forteo remains PA-eligible rather than flatly excluded in Michigan. Approvable under the same teriparatide PA program that covers Bonsity (2025 P 1033-17, eff 11/1/2025), but priced at the higher-cost 'E' tier rather than Bonsity's Tier 3.
Marked 'E, PA, SP' on the PDL -- same PA program and clinical criteria as Bonsity/Forteo, but placed at the higher-cost 'E' tier rather than Bonsity's Tier 3.

Not listed on the outpatient pharmacy PDL at all -- administered as a monthly in-office injection and billed under UHC's Commercial Medical Benefit Drug Policy for Evenity (Policy 2025D0080L, effective 12/1/2025, a national commercial policy). Requires diagnosis of postmenopausal osteoporosis at high fracture risk; treatment is limited to a maximum of 12 monthly doses because the anabolic effect wanes after that point.

records.stepTherapy: None of the anabolic agents in this class require a strict 'must-fail-bisphosphonate-first' step. PA criteria for both the teriparatide-group program and the Tymlos program accept EITHER a high-fracture-risk clinical profile (recent fracture, multiple risk factors, very low T-score, high fall risk, high FRAX score) OR documented failure/intolerance/contraindication to another osteoporosis therapy (e.g., alendronate, denosumab, risedronate, zoledronate) -- either path satisfies the medical-necessity criterion, so it functions as medical-necessity gating rather than mandatory sequential step therapy.
records.tier: Tier 3 - highest tier among agents actually listed on the pharmacy PDL for this class, plus PA and Specialty Pharmacy (SP) required (abaloparatide/TYMLOS)
records.verificationNote: Read the PDL's osteoporosis section directly (page footer '44', 0-indexed page 43; fetched at the assigned URL via WebFetch's saved raw PDF bytes, opened with PyMuPDF since the tool's own extraction returned only a 'corrupted/encoded' summary): TYMLOS (Tier 3, PA, SP), BONSITY (Tier 3, PA, SP), FORTEO (E, PA, SP), and generic 'teriparatide solution pen-injector 560mcg/2.24ml subcutaneous' (E, PA, SP) -- all four verbatim from the table. A full-document search for 'maryland' in the PDL returned zero hits, confirming no MD carve-out exists; because the FORTEO and generic-teriparatide lines carry an explicit 'PA' flag (not a bare 'E'), the national PA requirement applies in Michigan the same as everywhere else -- unlike the bare-'E' items in the oral-bisphosphonate and SERM classes, these are PA-eligible rather than non-formulary. Romosozumab/Evenity does not appear anywhere in the 80-page PDL (zero keyword hits for 'romosozumab' or 'evenity'), consistent with the PDL's stated scope exclusion for physician-office-administered drugs (page 3, 0-indexed); confirmed via WebSearch + WebFetch (again reading saved raw bytes with PyMuPDF) that Evenity is instead governed by a dedicated 'UnitedHealthcare Commercial Medical Benefit Drug Policy, Evenity (Romosozumab-Aqqg), Policy Number: 2025D0080L, Effective Date: December 1, 2025' -- a national commercial policy with zero hits for 'maryland' in its own text. Also fetched and read UHC's dedicated Tymlos PA/Notification document ('2025 P 1222-11', Effective 12/1/2025, at https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/prior-auth/drugs-pharmacy/commercial/r-z/PA-Notification-Tymlos.pdf) and the combined Bonsity/Forteo/Teriparatide-Injection PA/Notification document ('2025 P 1033-17', Effective 11/1/2025, at https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/prior-auth/drugs-pharmacy/commercial/a-g/PA-Notification-Forteo-Bonsity.pdf) directly -- both confirm verbatim the coverage-criteria structure (high fracture risk OR prior therapy failure, 2-year/24-month cumulative lifetime cap across all parathyroid hormone analogs) quoted above. TYMLOS was selected over Bonsity as the single class-level preferred agent because, on the PDL, abaloparatide has one clean Tier-3 listing while teriparatide is split across three entries (Forteo-E, Bonsity-Tier3, generic-E) with no explicit 'preferred' label distinguishing Bonsity from Tymlos in either the PDL or the two dedicated PA-notification documents -- this pick is a judgment call given the genuine near-tie in restriction level between Bonsity and Tymlos, disclosed here rather than presented as an unambiguous single preferred agent. The representative 80mcg/daily Tymlos dosing is standard FDA-label information, not stated in the UHC documents themselves. [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]

paRequired.reason: Marked 'E' alone with no separate PA/QL/SP flag. Michigan is not one of the three states (CT, NJ, NY) the document's footnote and legend name as having a Prior-Authorization fallback for bare 'E' items, so in Michigan this means excluded from coverage outright, not PA-eligible. The AB-rated generic raloxifene hcl is covered cleanly at Tier 2, reinforcing that the brand is a genuine non-formulary exclusion rather than a clearable barrier.

records.verificationNote: Fetched https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/resources/pharmacy/commercial-pdl-jan-2026.pdf directly (WebFetch's own summarizer returned only a 'corrupted/encoded' message per this repo's known uhcprovider.com quirk, but the tool result named the local path where it had already saved the raw PDF bytes; opening that path with PyMuPDF/fitz yielded full readable text across all 80 pages). Page 1 (0-indexed) confirms the document is UnitedHealthcare's '2026 Prescription Drug List,' Effective January 1, 2026, publisher 'UnitedHealthcare & affiliated companies.' The document names no state carve-out other than CT, NJ and NY. The 'Metabolic Bone Disease Agents - Drugs for Osteoporosis' section (page footer '44', 0-indexed page 43) lists, verbatim: raloxifene hcl (Tier 2, H-PA) and EVISTA (E, no other flag). Page 4 (0-indexed) supplies the symbol legend confirming H-PA = 'May be part of health care reform preventive with prior authorization' (a nationally-applicable flag, no state qualifier) and E = 'May be excluded from coverage or subject to Prior Authorization in Connecticut, New Jersey and New York' -- since Michigan isn't named in that three-state carve-out, EVISTA's bare 'E' flag means straightforward exclusion from coverage here. Only one SERM (raloxifene) is named in this class per the task scope, and it's the sole entry on the PDL for that mechanism -- no separate 'alternatives' exist within the SERM class itself. The representative 60mg once-daily strength/directions are standard FDA-label prescribing convention, not stated in the PDL (which lists drug names/tiers/flags only, no dosing guidance). [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]
